name: Determinism

subjectOf.text: The code is law paradigm departs from existing legal systems in three linked ways: it shifts authority from sovereign institutions to technical protocols, replaces interpretive flexibility with deterministic enforcement, and substitutes technological neutrality for normative deliberation.
subjectOf.abstract: fundamentally contrasts with existing legal systems by shifting authority from sovereign institutions to technical protocols, replacing interpretive flexibility with deterministic enforcement, and substituting normative deliberation with technological neutrality.
subjectOf.citation: Furrer Andreas, Wulf A. Kaal, Universal Digital Law Codex (UDLC) Building the Legal Infrastructure for the Digital Era (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5554218
scope_conditions: blockchain and smart contract architectures presented as self-sufficient regulation

subjectOf.text: The deterministic execution of smart contracts rigidly enforces coded terms and thereby incentivizes participants to exploit loopholes for immediate gain, because no mechanism exists to adapt the rules contextually.
subjectOf.abstract: Conversely, smart contracts' deterministic execution rigidly enforces coded terms, incentivizing participants to exploit loopholes for immediate gain, as there is no mechanism to adapt rules contextually.
subjectOf.citation: Furrer Andreas, Wulf A. Kaal, Universal Digital Law Codex (UDLC) Building the Legal Infrastructure for the Digital Era (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5554218
scope_conditions: smart contracts without on chain amendment or human review mechanisms

subjectOf.text: Smart contracts should incorporate clauses that trigger human review in cases of ambiguity, which secures equitable outcomes analogous to judicial discretion and counters the rigidity of deterministic execution.
subjectOf.abstract: For instance, smart contracts can incorporate clauses that trigger human review in cases of ambiguity, ensuring equitable outcomes akin to judicial discretion.
subjectOf.citation: Furrer Andreas, Wulf A. Kaal, Universal Digital Law Codex (UDLC) Building the Legal Infrastructure for the Digital Era (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5554218
scope_conditions: circumstances not anticipated in the code
